body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 적절한 것은?
While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash’s vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute.
solution: ② diagnosis (진단): '징후와 증상으로 질병이나 신체 상태를 식별하는 과정'이라는 뜻으로 영영 풀이가 정확하다. ① infectious (전염성의): 타인에게 전파될 수 없는 것이 아니라, '한 사람에게서 다른 사람에게로 전염될 수 있는(able to be passed from one person to another)'이라는 뜻이다. ③ bulky (부피가 큰, 뚱뚱한): 작고 휴대하기 쉬운 것이 아니라, '크고 무거워서 다루거나 옮기기 힘든(large and difficult to carry)'이라는 뜻이다. ④ affordable (가격이 알맞은, 감당할 수 있는): 매우 비싼 것이 아니라, '가격이 적당하여 돈을 지불할 만한(reasonably priced; cheap enough for most people to afford)'이라는 뜻이다. ⑤ take shape (형체를 갖추다, 구체화되다): 완전히 사라지는 것이 아니라, '구체적인 형태를 나타내거나 발전하기 시작하다(to start to develop into a clear or definite form)'라는 뜻이다. YBM(박) 4과 실전 모의고사 1회차
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사
choices: infectious : something that cannot be passed from one person to another.
diagnosis : the process of identifying a disease or condition from its signs and symptoms.
bulky : very small and easy to carry around.
affordable : extremely expensive and hard to pay for.
take shape : to disappear completely without leaving a trace. 1회차 실전 모의고사

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않은 것은?
Science for All Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash’s vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute.
solution: 본문에 따르면 Prakash가 발견한 현미경은 사용되지 않고 있었으며, 그 이유는 다음과 같다. bulky and awkward to transport (크고 운반하기 불편함) required training to operate (사용법 교육이 필요함) difficult to maintain (유지·관리가 어려움) delicate and expensive instrument (정교하고 비싼 장비) 따라서 "저렴하고, 휴대가 편리하며, 유지·관리가 쉬워 널리 사용되었다"는 ④의 내용은 본문과 일치하지 않는다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사
choices: Microscopes have played an important role in scientific research for more than 400 years.
The Foldscope was developed to provide an affordable alternative to conventional microscopes.
Prakash encountered an unused microscope for malaria testing while conducting research in Thailand in 2011.
The microscope Prakash found was widely used because it was inexpensive, portable, and easy to maintain.
Jim Cybulski became interested in the project because he wanted to use his engineering skills to make a positive impact on society. 1회차 실전 모의고사

answer: ⓐ experimented with ⓑ might have settled ⓒ were determined to create
solution: ⓐ 앞뒤 문장이 모두 과거시제로 서술되며, Prakash와 Cybulski가 적절한 절충안을 찾기 위해 '다양한 설계와 재료를 실험해 보았다'는 의미이므로, 전치사 with와 결합한 동사구 experimented with가 알맞다. ⓑ 'While(반면에)'로 시작하는 양보의 부사절 안에서, 많은 제조업체들이 두 극단 사이의 중간 지점에 '안주했을지도 모른다'는 과거 사실에 대한 추측을 나타내야 하므로, 조동사 might와 현재완료 have settled가 결합한 might have settled가 알맞다. ⓒ 주절에서 Prakash와 Cybulski가 저렴하면서도 고성능인 현미경을 만들기로 '결심했다'는 의미이며, 'be determined to+동사원형(~하기로 결심하다)' 구조의 수동태이므로 were determined to create가 알맞다.

body:
다음 중 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 공통으로 들어갈 말은?
The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. (A) , the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high-resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. (B) , over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski had given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges.Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.
solution: (A)와 (B) 뒤의 문장은 모두 앞 문장에 새로운 장점이나 추가 정보를 덧붙이는 내용이다. (A)에서는 Foldscope의 휴대성과 가벼움을 설명한 뒤, 추가적으로 내구성이 뛰어나다는 내용을 덧붙이고 있다. (B)에서는 가짜 약 판별 사례를 설명한 뒤, 추가적으로 과학 논문과 연구 프로젝트 사례를 소개하고 있다. 따라서 두 빈칸 모두 ‘게다가, 더욱이’의 의미를 가진 첨가 표현이 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다. ② In the end : ‘결국’라는 뜻으로 결론이나 마지막 결과를 나타낼 때 사용한다. ③ As a result : ‘그 결과’라는 뜻으로 원인과 결과 관계를 나타낸다. ④ On the other hand : ‘반면에’라는 뜻으로 대조 관계를 나타낸다. ⑤ In other words : ‘즉, 다시 말해’라는 뜻으로 앞 내용을 바꾸어 설명할 때 사용한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사

Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the benefit of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers was established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone to access their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. Scientists’ efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now expanding to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals. Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. ⓐ(현미경이 발명되지 않았다면 우리는 박테리아 를 발견하지 못했을지도 모른다 / might, if, microscopes) or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. "The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash (A)came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
(A) It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that ⓐhis idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. ㉠A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. ㉡Stanford University is a prestigious one that ranks at the top in the United States. After hearing Prakash's ⓑvision, Cybulski quickly recognized ⓒits potential and was eager to contribute.
(B) For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. ㉢These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. ㉣The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving ⓓit closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen.
(C) An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. ㉤However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create ⓔa microscope that was both inexpensive and high- performing, while remaining accessible to all.

윗글 (C)의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
solution: Prakash와 Cybulski가 모든 사람이 접근 가능한 현미경을 만들기 위해 다양한 재료와 디자인으로 실험했다는 내용의 글이다. 따라서 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은 ③ 'Prakash와 Cybulski 저렴하고 고성능의 현미경을 만들기 위해 다양한 디자인과 재료를 시도했다.'이다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
ⓐAfter drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. (가)
The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times,
ⓑmaking it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. (나)
It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. (다)
Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, ⓒallowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high-resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries,
ⓓmaking it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five.
ⓔWhen crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. ⒶIf Prakash and Cybulski had given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges. Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.

윗글의 밑줄 친 Ⓐ의 의미를 표현한 것 중, 가장 적절한 것은?
solution: Ⓐ는 가정법 과거완료 문장으로, 과거에 포기하지 않았기 때문에 이러한 성취가 일어났음을 드러낸다. 따라서 가장 적절하게 표현한 것은 ①이다.

solution: ⑤ gave up → had given up 결과절에 "could not have occurred"(조동사 과거형 + have + 과거분사)가 쓰여 가정법 과거완료 구문임을 나타낸다. 가정법 과거완료에서 if절은 반드시 「had + 과거분사」 형태여야 하므로, gave up(단순 과거)을 had given up으로 고쳐야 한다. 문맥상 Prakash와 Cybulski가 과거에 아이디어를 포기했더라면이라는 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 것이므로 if절과 결과절 모두 가정법 과거완료로 일치시켜야 한다. 따라서 ⑤가 정답이다. ① settled on: '~로 결정하다'라는 뜻의 구동사 settle on이 과거 시제로 올바르게 쓰였다. ② weighs: Foldscope의 일반적 특성(무게)을 나타내는 현재 시제 단수 동사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ allowing: 앞 절 전체의 내용을 의미상 주어로 취하며 결과를 나타내는 현재분사 allowing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ When crushed: 주어인 real drugs(약품)가 분쇄되는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 crushed가 접속사 When과 함께 올바르게 쓰였다. 2. if절은 수동태로, 주절은 능동태로 쓸 것
3. <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (형태 변형 가 능, 필요시 단어 추가 가능).

5. 대문자 및 마침표에 유의하여 쓸 것
보기 if / microscope / not / invent / we / might / not / discover / bacteria / or / microscopic / structure / living / organism
→ _____ .
answer: If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
solution: 만약 ~하지 않았다면, …했을지도 모른다'라는 과거 사실에 반대되는 가정을 나타내야 하므로 가정법 과거완료를 사용한다. if절은 'If + 주어(microscopes) + had not been + 과거분사(invented)'로 쓰는데, 현미경이 '발명되는' 수동의 대상이므로 수동태로 쓴다. 주절은 'we might not have + 과거분사(discovered)'로 쓰고, 목적어로 'bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms'를 연결하여 '박테리아나 생물체의 미세한 구조'라는 의미를 완성한다.

Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the (A) [ benefit / detriment ] of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more (B) [ exorbitant / affordable ], some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers was established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone to access their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. Scientists’ efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now (C) [ shrinking / expanding ] to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals.

(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문을 모두 고르면? (정답 2 개)
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
① How long have microscopes been used as a tool in science?
② What material was primarily used to make the Foldscope?
③ In what year did Prakash come across the unused, expensive microscope?
④ How many Foldscopes were distributed in Thailand by the end of 2011?
⑤ What was the total budget allocated for the Foldscope research project?
solution: ④ 2011년 말까지 태국에 배포된 Foldscope의 개수는 본문에 전혀 언급되지 않았으므로 답할 수 없다. ⑤ Foldscope 연구 프로젝트에 배정된 총예산 규모는 본문에서 전혀 다루지 않으므로 답할 수 없다. ① 현미경이 400년 넘게 과학의 필수 도구였다고 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ② Foldscope가 '종이(paper)' 현미경이라고 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ③ Prakash가 방치된 현미경을 발견한 시점이 2011년이라고 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사

While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
solution: ② 특정 지역에서는 비용 때문에 기본 광학 현미경조차 접근할 수 없다고 명시했으므로 일치한다. ① Foldscope는 Prakash와 Cybulski가 함께 발명했다고 했으므로, 혼자 발명했다는 설명은 일치하지 않는다. ③ Foldscope는 '강력한 배율을 달성했다고(achieved powerful magnification)' 명시했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ④ Prakash가 Foldscope로 박테리아를 처음 발견했다는 내용은 본문에 없으며, 박테리아 발견은 현미경 발명 전반에 대한 일반적 언급일 뿐이므로 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 그 현미경은 '치료(treating)'가 아니라 말라리아 '검사 (testing)'를 위한 것이었으므로 일치하지 않는다.

다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 글의 흐름상 어휘의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 모두 고르면? (정답 2개)
Microscopes have been an ⓐvital tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of ⓑliving organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost
ⓒmore than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was ⓓutilized. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its
ⓔspread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
solution: ⓒ more than → less than 바로 뒤에서 Prakash가 '과학을 모두에게 접근 가능하게 만드는 것이 목표였다'고 말하는 흐름과, Foldscope가 저비용 해결책으로 제시되었다는 문맥상, 부품 비용이 '1달러 이상'이 아니라 '1달러 미만'이어야 알맞다. ⓓ utilized → unused 바로 뒤 문장에서 '그렇다면 왜 그 현미경은 사용되지 않은 채 방치되어 있었을까?(why was the microscope sitting unused?)'라는 질문이 이어지므로, 앞 문장에서도 그 현미경이 '활용되었다(utilized)'가 아니라 '사용되지 않았다 (unused)'고 해야 문맥이 일관된다. ⓐ vital: 필수적인 ⓑ living: 살아있는 ⓔ spread: 확산
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. ⓐIt was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges while their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making ⓑit capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. ⓒIt is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by ⓓits compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light. ⓔIt is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. ⓐIt was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges while their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making ⓑit capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. ⓒIt is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by ⓓits compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light. ⓔIt is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide.

밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 it(It)의 쓰임이 다른 하나는?
solution: ⓐ는 paper를, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 The Foldscope를 지칭하지만, ⓔ의 It은 가주어로 쓰였다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한것은?
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, (A) _____ , even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. (B) _____ , the Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. "The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. (C) , malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
solution: (A) 앞 문단에서 현미경이 과학의 필수 도구였다는 긍정적 진술이 나온 뒤, 뒤에서는 일부 지역에서 기본 현미경조차 접근할 수 없다는 상반된 상황이 이어지므로, 대조를 나타내는 'Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)'가 알맞다. (B) 앞 문장에서 Foldscope가 '해결책으로 제시되었다'는 일반적 진술이 나온 뒤, 뒤에서는 그것이 구체적으로 어떤 성능과 비용을 달성했는지 부연 설명하므로, 구체화를 나타내는 'In particular(구체적으로 말하면)'가 알맞다. (C) 앞 문장에서 말라리아 검사용 현미경이 방치되어 있었다는 사실이 나온 뒤, 뒤에서는 말라리아의 심각성(연간 50만 명 이상 사망)을 제시하며 그 방치가 왜 문제인지를 뒷받침하므로, 강조·부연을 나타내는 'Indeed(실제로)'가 알맞다. 따라서, ① Nevertheless - In particular - Indeed 가 정답으로 가장 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable (A) [compromise / competition]. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both (B) [inexpensive / exorbitant] and high-performing, while ⓐremaining accessible to all. After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many (C) [breakthroughs / challenges] during their attempts ⓑto develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they ⓒsettled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and ⓓnaming their invention the Foldscope.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 하나 골라 기호를 쓰고, 그 이유를 서술한 뒤 올바른 표현으로 고쳐 쓰시오.
( ), _____ → 이유:
answer: ⓓ naming→ named 주어 'they' 뒤에 동사 'settled on'과 'named'가 'and'를 통 해 병렬구조로 이어져 있으므로 'named'가 적절하다.
solution: ⓓ naming→ named 주어 'they' 뒤에 동사 'settled on'과 'named'가 'and'를 통해 병렬구조로 이어져 있으므로 'named'가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사

body:
다음 밑줄 친 우리말의 의미를 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski had given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, 과학은 이러한 문제들에 대한 해결책을 찾는 데 있어 중요한 역할 을 하고 있다. Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.
조건 1. 현재진행형(be동사+동사원형ing)을 사용할것
2. 'in+동명사(~하는 데 있어)' 구조를 사용할 것
3. <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (형태 변형 가능).
4. 12단어로 쓸 것
5. 대문자 및 마침표에 유의하여 쓸 것
보기 science / play / a / crucial / role / in / find / solution / to / these / challenge
→ _____ .
answer: science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges
solution: 주어 science와 현재진행형 동사 is playing을 쓰고, 목적어 'a crucial role(중요한 역할)'을 연결한다. 이어서 '~하는 데 있어'라는 의미의 전치사 in 뒤에 동명사 finding을 쓰고, 그 목적어인 solutions to these challenges(이러한 문제들에 대한 해결책)를 배열하여 문장을 완성한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사

After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. ⓐIt was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making ⓑit capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. ⓒIts usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making ⓓit an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, ⓔit has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs.
solution: ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 The Foldscope를 가리키지만, ⓐ는 paper를 가리킨다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. (가)현미경이 발명되지 않았다면 우리는 박테리아 나 생명체의 미세한 구조를 발견하지 못했을지도 모른다. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. (A) It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. (B)
"The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. (C) But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. (D) A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. Meeting Jim Cybulski was the turning point that brought his vision of an affordable and accessible microscope to life. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. (A) It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. (B)
"The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. (C) But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. (D) A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. Meeting Jim Cybulski was the turning point that brought his vision of an affordable and accessible microscope to life. (E) A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash's vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute.

There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as . Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. "The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling." Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential.

다음 The Foldscope에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는것은?
The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, using Foldscope data, over 400 scientific papers have been published and around 1,200 various projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski had given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred.

Science for All Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash.
solution: ① microscope (현미경): 종이나 천을 자르는 도구가 아니라, '육안으로 볼 수 없는 아주 작은 물체나 생물을 확대해서 보여주는 광학 기구(A device that uses lenses to make very small objects look larger)'를 뜻합니다. (선택지의 설명은 가위나 칼에 가깝다.) ② structure (구조): 어떤 것의 여러 부분이 배열되거나 조직되어 있는 방식으로 올바른 풀이다. ③ organism (유기체, 생물): 동물, 식물, 박테리아와 같이 살아 있는 생명체를 뜻하므로 올바른 풀이다. ④ accessible (이용 가능한, 접근하기 쉬운): 쉽게 도달하거나 사용할 수 있는 상태를 뜻하므로 올바른 풀이다. ⑤ magnification (확대): 물체를 실제보다 더 크게 보이게 만드는 과정이나 기능으로 올바른 풀이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 실전 모의고사
choices: microscope : a small tool used to cut paper or fabric.
structure : the way in which parts of something are arranged or organized.
organism : a living thing, such as an animal, plant, or bacteria.
accessible : able to be reached or used easily.
magnification : the process of making an object appear larger than it really is.

For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube ⓐwhich the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually ⓑaccomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order ⓒto find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were ⓓdetermined to create a microscope that was both inexpensive and high-performing, while remaining accessible to all. After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and ⓔwide available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope.

For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. ⓐThe microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. ⓑFinally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component.
ⓒHowever, such a microscope would likely be enormous expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable compromise. ⓓWhile many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both inexpensive and high-performing, while remained accessible to all. After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. ⓔUltimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope.
solution: 정답: (1) ⓒ, enormous → enormously (2) ⓓ, remained → remaining

The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. ⓐMoreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. ⓑIt is also possible to project a high-resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide.
ⓒThe Foldscope has been utilizing for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub- Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. ⓓIf Prakash and Cybulski have given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred.
ⓔAs billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges. Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.

solution: 8 million Foldscopes(복수)이므로, 현재완료 수동태의 be동사도 복수형 have가 되어야 알맞다. ⓐ 앞 내용(140배 배율 제공)이 초래하는 결과를 부가적으로 설명하는 분사구문으로 알맞다. ⓑ '오래가도록' 만들어졌다는 의미로 형용사 built를 수식하는 to부정사의 부사적 용법으로 알맞다. ⓒ 앞 내용(휴대폰 카메라와의 호환성)이 초래하는 결과를 부가적으로 설명하는 분사구문으로 알맞다. ⓓ 가주어 It, 진주어 to부정사 구조(It is possible to부정사) 에 맞게 쓰였으므로 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전
choices: It was in high school that the book changed his life.

body:
다음 문장과 의미가 통하는 가정법 문장을 고르시오.
They won the game only because their coach trained them hard.
solution: 제시문은 '코치가 열심히 훈련시켰기 때문에 경기에서 이겼다'는 실제 사실을 나타낸다. 이를 가정법 과거완료로 바꾸면 '코치가 열심히 훈련시키지 않았다면 이기지 못했을 것이다'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 ③이 정답이다. ①은 미래 조건문이므로 시제가 맞지 않다. ②는 가정법 과거로 현재의 반대를 나타내므로 틀리다. ④는 훈련시키지 않았어도 이겼을 것이라는 반대의 의미이므로 틀리다. ⑤는 실제로 훈련시키지 않은 것으로 오해하게 하는 반대의 의미이므로 틀리다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전
choices: They will win the game if their coach trains them hard.
They would win the game if their coach trained them hard.
If their coach hadn't trained them hard, they wouldn't have won the game.
If their coach hadn't trained them hard, they would have won the game.
They would have won the game if their coach had trained them hard.

solution: 제시문은 '선생님이 매일 지도해 주었기 때문에 시험에 합격했다'는 실제 있었던 일을 나타낸다. 이를 가정법 과거완료로 바꾸면 실제와 반대되는 상황, 즉 '선생님이 지도해 주지 않았다면 합격하지 못했을 것이다'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 ②가 정답이다. ①은 미래를 나타내는 조건문이므로 시제가 맞지 않다. ③은 가정법 과거로 현재 사실의 반대를 나타내므로 적절하지 않다. ④는 지도해 주지 않았어도 합격했을 것이라는 반대의 의미이므로 틀리다. ⑤는 실제로 지도해 주지 않은 것으로 오해하게 하는 반대의 의미이므로 틀리다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전
choices: She will pass the exam if her teacher tutors her every day.

If her teacher hadn't tutored her every day, she would have passed the exam.

solution: ④ I had known → If I had known 현재 문장은 조건을 나타내는 접속사 If가 빠져 있으므로 If I had known the answer, I would have raised my hand.로 고쳐야 한다. ① It is time + 주어 + 과거동사는 ‘이제 ~해야 할 때이다’ 라는 뜻을 나타내므로 적절하다. ② A wise investor가 가정의 조건을 대신하여 ‘현명한 투자자라면’이라는 의미를 나타내므로 적절하다. ③ If + 주어 + 과거동사, 주어 + would + 동사원형의 가정법 과거 구조이므로 적절하다. ⑤ as if 뒤에 주절보다 앞선 상황을 나타내는 과거완료 had solved가 쓰였으므로 적절하다.

body:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ 중, 어법상 틀린 것의 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
Education shapes our future paths, and my career ⓐwould have developed differently if I had chosen different subjects. If I ⓑstudied medicine when I was younger, I could become a doctor now. But if I ⓒhadn't found my passion for teaching, I wouldn't have become an educator.
solution: 과거에 대한 가정을 나타내는 if절에서는 가정법 과거완료(had + 과거분사)를 써야 하므로 'studied'를 'had studied'로 고쳐야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법상 옳은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
• If he (A)[exercised / had exercised] regularly, he would have stayed healthy.
• The flowers (B)[would / would not] have died if they had been watered properly.
• If you didn't check the weather forecast, there could (C)[be / have been] unexpected rain.
solution: (A)는 가정법 과거완료의 조건절이므로 'had exercised'가 적절하고, (B)는 적절히 물을 주었다면 꽃이 죽지 않았을 것이므로 'would not'이 적절하며, (C)는 가정법 과거의 주절에서 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형 'be'가 적절하므로 정답은 ④이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법상 옳은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

• The project (B)[would / would not] have succeeded if the team had worked together efficiently.

(B) would 문맥상 팀이 효율적으로 함께 일했다면 프로젝트가 성공했을 것이라는 의미가 되어야 하므로, 긍정을 나타내는 would를 쓰는 것이 올바르다. body:
다음 중 어법에 맞지 않는 두 문장을 찾아 각각 틀린 부분을 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
ⓐThe food that otherwise would have been wasted is distributed to shelters.
ⓑIf she had studied the map, she would find the shortcut.
ⓒIf the engineer had checked the bridge, it might be stable today.
ⓓI wish I practiced more during my time on the team. 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ → 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ →
answer: ⓑ: would find → would have found, ⓓ: practiced → had practiced
solution: b는 if절이 'had studied'로 가정법 과거완료인데, 주절에 현재 시점 부사가 없음에도 'would find'처럼 단순 형태로 쓰여 시제가 어긋난다. 주절은 'would have found'로 써야 한다. d는 wish 뒤에 'during my time on the team'이라는 특정 과거 시점에 대한 아쉬움을 나타내므로 과거완료 'had practiced'가 와야 하는데 단순과거 'practiced'가 쓰여 틀렸다. a는 실제로 일어난 일과 대조되는 가정법 과거완료 'otherwise would have been wasted'가 올바르게 쓰였고, c는 과거의 조건이 현재까지 영향을 미치는 혼합 가정법으로 'might be stable today'가 올바르게 쓰여 옳은 문장이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법에 맞지 않는 두 문장을 찾아 각각 틀린 부분을 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
ⓐIf the rescue team had arrived sooner, the hikers might be safe now.
ⓑDocuments that otherwise would have been destroyed are preserved in the archive.
ⓒIf he had trained harder last month, he would win the championship.
ⓓI wish I studied harder during my last year in college. 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ → 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ →
answer: ⓒ: would win → would have won, ⓓ: studied → had studied
solution: c는 if절이 'had trained'로 과거 사실의 반대를 나타내는 가정법 과거완료인데, 주절에 now나 today 같은 현재 부사가 없음에도 'would win'처럼 단순 형태로 쓰여 시제가 어긋난다. 혼합 가정법이 아니므로 주절도 'would have won'으로 써야 한다. d는 wish 뒤에 'during my last year in college'라는 특정 과거 시점에 대한 아쉬움을 나타내므로 'had studied'와 같은 과거완료가 와야 하는데 단순과거 'studied'가 쓰여 틀렸다. a는 과거의 조건이 현재까지 영향을 미치는 혼합 가정법으로 'might be safe now'가 올바르게 쓰였고, b는 실제로 일어난 일과 대조되는 가정법 과거완료 'otherwise would have been destroyed'가 올바르게 쓰여 옳은 문장이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐIf it had not been for his warning, they couldn't have avoided the accident.
ⓑIt is crucial that the team submitted the report by Monday.
ⓒHe speaks as if he had traveled across South America.
ⓓYou would be happier right now if you were less anxious.
ⓔThey would have finished the race if they trained harder.
ⓕIt is time that each employee took ownership of their tasks.
solution: b와 e가 어법상 틀린 문장이므로 정답은 ②이다. b에서 'It is crucial that' 뒤에는 당위성을 나타내는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 submit이 되어야 하는데 과거형 submitted를 써서 틀렸다. e에서 'would have finished'라는 과거완료 형태의 결과가 왔으므로 조건절도 과거완료인 'had trained'가 되어야 하는데 단순과거 trained를 써서 시제가 어긋난다. a는 'If it had not been for + 명사, S + couldn't have p.p.' 형태의 가정법 과거완료로 올바르다. c는 'as if + had p.p.'로 과거 사실과 다른 상황을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다. d는 'If + were, S + would + 동사원형' 형태의 가정법 과거로 올바르다. f는 'It is time that + S + 과거형'으로 당위성을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐIf it had not been for the storm, we could have arrived earlier.
ⓑIt is important that the manager attended the conference.
ⓒThey talk as if they had lived in Paris for years.
ⓓWe would be there right now if we were more prepared.
ⓔShe would have accepted the offer if she had more time.
ⓕIt is time that every citizen took part in the election.
solution: b와 e가 어법상 틀린 문장이므로 정답은 ⑤이다. b에서 'It is important that' 뒤에는 당위성을 나타내는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 attend가 되어야 하는데 과거형 attended를 써서 틀렸다. e에서 'would have accepted'라는 과거완료 형태의 결과가 왔으므로 조건절도 과거완료인 'had had'가 되어야 하는데 단순과거 had를 써서 시제가 어긋난다. a는 'If it had not been for + 명사, S + could have p.p.' 형태의 가정법 과거완료로 올바르다. c는 'as if + had p.p.'로 과거 사실과 다른 상황을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다. d는 'If + were, S + would + 동사원형' 형태의 가정법 과거로 올바르다. f는 'It is time that + S + 과거형'으로 당위성을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 맞는 문장의 개수는?
ⓐIf she practiced every day, she would improve quickly.
ⓑHe describes the plan as if it were flawless.
ⓒThey double-checked the equipment before the launch; otherwise, the mission could have failed disastrously.
ⓓIf the team had started the project earlier, it would be completed by now.
ⓔI wish I were more patient so that I could handle stressful situations calmly.
ⓕIf it had not been for her quick thinking, the patient would have died during the surgery.
solution: 여섯 문장 모두 어법상 올바르다. a는 가정법 과거(If+과거동사, would+동사원형)으로 현재 사실에 반대되는 상황을 올바르게 나타낸다. b는 'as if+가정법 과거(were)'로 실제와 다른 상황을 비유하는 올바른 표현이다. c는 실제로 일어난 과거 행동(double-checked) 뒤에 otherwise를 이용해 그렇지 않았다면 일어났을 과거의 결과를 'could have+p.p.'로 나타낸 올바른 문장이다. d는 'had started'라는 과거완료 조건과 현재를 나타내는 'by now'에 어울리게 결과절에서 'would be completed'를 사용하여 시제가 올바르게 일치한다. e는 'wish+가정법 과거(were)' 뒤에 'so that+could'로 현재 능력에 대한 소망을 나타내는 올바른 문장이다. f는 'If it had not been for'로 과거 사실에 반대되는 상황을 나타내고, 결과절에서도 'would have died'와 'during the surgery'라는 과거 시점이 일치하므로 올바르다. YBM(박) 4과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 맞는 문장의 개수는?
ⓐIf they left now, they would arrive before sunset.
ⓑHe behaves as if he were the manager of the store.
ⓒShe backed up her files regularly; otherwise, she would have lost all her data in the crash.
ⓓIf the scientists had discovered the vaccine sooner, thousands of lives would have been saved by now.
ⓔI wish I had studied harder so that I could pass the exam now.
ⓕIf it were not for the traffic jam, she would have arrived on time yesterday.
solution: 어법상 맞는 문장은 a, b, c로 총 3개다. a는 가정법 과거(If+과거동사, would+동사원형)으로 현재 사실에 반대되는 상황을 올바르게 나타낸다. b는 'as if+가정법 과거(were)'로 실제와 다른 상황을 비유하는 올바른 표현이다. c는 반복적으로 일어난 과거 행동(backed up) 뒤에 otherwise를 이용해 그렇지 않았다면 일어났을 과거의 결과를 'would have+p.p.'로 나타낸 올바른 문장이다. d는 'had discovered'라는 과거완료 조건에 대해 결과절에서 'would have been saved'(과거 완료 조동사) 를 쓰면서 'by now'라는 현재 시점 표현을 함께 써서 시제가 어긋난다. 'by now'와 어울리려면 'would be saved'로 써야 한다. e는 'wish+had studied'로 과거에 대한 후회를 나타냈는데, 결과절에서 'could pass...now'처럼 현재 시점을 나타내는 표현을 써서 시제가 맞지 않는다. 과거의 결과를 나타내려면 'could have passed the exam'으로 써야 한다. f는 'If it were not for'는 현재 사실에 반대되는 상황을 나타내는 표현인데 결과절에 'yesterday'라는 명백한 과거 시점이 나와 시제가 맞지 않는다. 과거 사실에 반대되는 상황을 나타내려면 'If it had not been for'를 써야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body: 밑줄 친 부분이 문법과 문맥상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
solution: ⑤ hired → had hired 주절의 동사가 'would have p.p'인 것으로 보아 과거의 일을 가정하는 문장이므로 주절의 동사는 'had p.p' 형태여야 한다.

body:
주어진 문장과 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 같은 것을 고르시오.

body:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법 또는 문맥상 틀린 것끼리 짝지 어진 것을 고르시오.
• If the fire ⓐspread to the forest, the damage would have been enormous.
• If they could afford it, they ⓑwould be able to buy a new house.
• But for modern medicine, many patients
ⓒwould have to suffer from diseases.
• If she had prepared better, she ⓓcould have more confidence today.
• If we had left earlier, we ⓔwould have missed the train.
• The project would have failed ⓕhad it not been for the team leader.
solution: ⓐ는 가정법 과거 완료 구문으로 'If 주어 과거완료 ~, 주어 조동사의 과거형 have 과거분사~'형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 spread를 had spread로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ더 일찍 떠났더라면 기차를 놓치지 않았을 것이라는 흐름이 문맥상 자연스럽다. 따라서 'would have missed'를 'wouldn't have missed'로 고쳐야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
주어진 문장과 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 같은 것을 고르시오.
보기 It was Sarah that completed the project yesterday.
solution: 주어진 문장의 'It'은 'Sarah'를 강조하는 'it was ~ that' 구문에 쓰인 'it'이다. 선택지 중에서는 ①의 'It'이 'cancer'을 강조하는 강조구문이다.

Lucy Bennett, a retired elementary school teacher, ⓐused to call her grandchildren every weekend, but they rarely picked up the phone. One day, her son told her that the kids were busy with exams and rarely answered calls. Lucy said, “If I ⓑwill send them a letter, I will surely get a reply.” She wrote two cheerful letters to the grandchildren and mentioned that she could not but ⓒto feel excited to send each of them a surprise gift: a new bicycle voucher. Then she mailed the letters, but forgot to enclose the vouchers. Within a week she received warm letters from both grandchildren, who noted at the end that she had forgotten to include the voucher. If the voucher ⓓhad been included, would they

While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
① Had microscopes not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.

When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology ⓑcreating artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers
ⓒwas established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone ⓓaccess their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they ⓐsettled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. 실전 학습 The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, ⓑweighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, ⓒallowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light.
It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five.
ⓓWhen crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski
ⓔgave up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges. Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.
solution: ⑤ gave up → had given up 결과절에 "could not have occurred"(조동사 과거형 + have + 과거분사)가 쓰여 가정법 과거완료 구문임을 나타낸다. 가정법 과거완료에서 if절은 반드시 「had + 과거분사」 형태여야 하므로, gave up(단순 과거)을 had given up으로 고쳐야 한다. 문맥상 Prakash와 Cybulski가 과거에 아이디어를 포기했더라면이라는 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 것이므로 if절과 결과절 모두 가정법 과거완료로 일치시켜야 한다. 따라서 ⑤가 정답이다. ① settled on: '~로 결정하다'라는 뜻의 구동사 settle on이 과거 시제로 올바르게 쓰였다. ② weighs: Foldscope의 일반적 특성(무게)을 나타내는 현재 시제 단수 동사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ allowing: 앞 절 전체의 내용을 의미상 주어로 취하며 결과를 나타내는 현재분사 allowing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ When crushed: 주어인 real drugs(약품)가 분쇄되는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 crushed가 접속사 When과 함께 올바르게 쓰였다.
